title: Copilot Studio: Dataverse tables as a native knowledge source for agents
summary: Hold: Microsoft documents that Dataverse knowledge answers respect the asking user's access, contrary to the briefing's stated uncertainty. The briefing also leaves published billing and storage rules unresolved and needs to distinguish standard-harness licence inclusions from Microsoft Copilot harness consumption.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans to enable Dataverse as native knowledge for agents grounded in structured enterprise and business data.
claims.quote: We are enabling Microsoft Dataverse as a native knowledge source in Copilot Studio, expanding the platform’s ability to ground AI agents in structured enterprise data.

claims.where: Why it matters; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft has not specified automatic maker rollout of this roadmap change or a separate feature-specific availability switch.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse knowledge enable admin default rollout; Dataverse knowledge source tenant-wide switch; 568929 rollout. Opened both Dataverse knowledge guides and Configure Dataverse search; found the search prerequisite, not a separate feature switch or automatic rollout statement.

claims.claim: No source says the roadmap change automatically changes existing agents.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse knowledge enable admin default rollout; 568929 Dataverse Copilot Studio rollout. Opened both feature guides and read the record; they describe adding sources, not automatic modification of existing agents.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Dataverse search respects Dataverse security roles and permissions.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn does not say whose permissions apply when an end user asks an agent about Dataverse knowledge.
claims.quote: Agent user authentication for knowledge sources means that when a specific user asks a question of the agent, the agent only surfaces content that the specific user can access.
claims.fix: Replace the uncertainty with: 'For Dataverse knowledge, Learn lists the agent user's Microsoft Entra ID authentication and says the agent only surfaces content that the asking user can access.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/knowledge-copilot-studio#supported-knowledge-sources. Remove the corresponding open question; change the checklist's permission-confirmation clause to 'verify the intended users can access the selected records'.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls

claims.quote: Turning off Dataverse search deprovisions and removes the index within 12 hours.

claims.quote: If you turn on Dataverse search after it's been off for 12 hours, it creates a fresh index that needs to go through a full sync.

claims.claim: The Dataverse knowledge documentation describes grounding answers, not a write action.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse knowledge source write Copilot Studio. Opened both Dataverse knowledge guides and Configure Dataverse search; the knowledge instructions describe retrieval and grounding, with no write operation for the knowledge source.

claims.quote: Copilot Credits are the unit that measures agent usage. You calculate the total cost based on the sum of the Copilot Credits your organization uses.

claims.claim: The licensing model is mixed, combining consumption with eligible subscription-included employee usage.
claims.quote: Employee-facing usage scenarios (Business to Employee) of Copilot Studio agents and Copilot Studio tools and features that these agents invoke are included in the Microsoft Copilot USL

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No separate Dataverse-knowledge-specific credit rate or price is published in the billing documentation checked.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse knowledge billing Copilot Credits generative answers. Opened Billing rates and management and Overview of usage-based billing; neither lists a separate Dataverse knowledge rate. This does not negate the published general billing rules.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Meter; Open questions
claims.claim: Whether answers grounded in Dataverse tables bill as generative answers remains undocumented.
claims.quote: All knowledge sources that you add at the agent level are added to the generative answers node in the Conversational boosting system topic.
claims.fix: Replace the billing uncertainty and its open question with: 'For standard-harness agents, Dataverse is a supported generative-answers knowledge source. The published generative-answer feature rate is 2 Copilot Credits; other applicable feature or reasoning-model charges can also apply. Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/knowledge-copilot-studio, https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/requirements-messages-management and https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/billing-credit-overview.

claims.claim: Employee-facing usage is included when the user has Microsoft Copilot and the agent uses that authenticated identity, without distinguishing harnesses.

Usage by agents powered by the Microsoft Copilot harness is not included with a user's Microsoft 365 Copilot licence.' Cite the existing Billing rates and management and Govern Copilot Credit consumption sources.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Caps; controls[1]; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Admins can set monthly consumption limits for individual Copilot Studio agents.
claims.quote: Admins can set monthly consumption limits for each Copilot Studio agent, regardless of whether the environment uses prepaid capacity or pay-as-you-go billing.

claims.claim: Per-agent limit notifications can alert environment and tenant admins as usage approaches the limit.
claims.quote: Notifications: Admins, both at the environment and tenant level, receive alerts when an agent's usage approaches the defined limit.

claims.claim: A configurable hard stop turns the agent off at its defined monthly limit.
claims.quote:
After you set limits, you can configure two key guardrails:
Hard stop: The agent is automatically turned off once it hits the defined limit.

claims.claim: Agent consumption limits are not applied instantly.
claims.quote: Limits aren't applied instantly. An agent can continue to respond for some time after it reaches its limit, so set limits and notification thresholds with some margin.
